messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.mesh.create having tough time to converge?
parts:
Hi,
you've stumbled on one of the hard-to-fix bugs in the meshing
software: It doesn't always detect when the input data generates a
non-unique Delaunay triangulation, which then sometimes leads to an
infinite loop where a single edge is flipped back and forth, between
two equally "good" triangulations. This is what happens for your very
regularly placed data. If you are on Linux (perhaps also Mac), you
can see what's happening by adding plot.delay=1 to the
inla.mesh.create command.

One solution is to make very small random perturbations to the input data.
In your case, it turns out that it is enough to shift the values by a
common amount, even something as simple as "+1". At least on my
computer, the following works:

loc = as.matrix(read.table("s.txt")) ## Read the data
mesh = inla.mesh.create(loc+1, ...) ## Shift input to avoid numerical
ambiguity problems in fmesher
mesh$loc = mesh$loc-1 ## Shift the output back again.

/Finn
